name: Shin-ei Uni-Vibe (Univox, c. 1968)
description: Shin-ei Uni-Vibe (Univox / Unicord model 905, late 1960s), mains powered. Supply: about 16 Vrms secondary, one rectifier diode into 1000 µF (≈ 21 V for the LFO and lamp), then 470 Ω / 220 µF / 470 Ω / 220 µF to the ≈ 16-17 V audio rail. Preamp: input 22 kΩ mixing resistors and 47 kΩ, then a three-transistor discrete 'op-amp' (Q1 2SC539 with 1.2 MΩ collector load and 1.2 MΩ DC feedback, Q2 with 47 kΩ / 6.8 kΩ ∥ 1 µF and the 330 pF compensation cap, Q3 phase splitter with 4.7 kΩ collector and 3.3 kΩ + 1.2 kΩ split emitter feeding back to Q1's emitter: gain ≈ 3.75). Four phase stages, each fed by a phase cap from the previous collector and a 1 µF block cap + LDR + 4.7 kΩ from the previous emitter; Cp = 15 nF, 220 nF, 470 pF, 4.7 nF. Stages 1-3: bootstrapped 100 kΩ bias from a 100 kΩ / 47 kΩ divider into a Darlington-fed phase splitter (4.7 kΩ / 4.7 kΩ); stage 4: a single emitter follower (68 kΩ / 47 kΩ divider, 22 kΩ emitter). Output mixer: Chorus = dry (preamp emitter) and wet 100 kΩ each; Vibrato = wet through 47 kΩ / 220 kΩ; 100 kΩ Volume. LFO: Darlington phase-shift oscillator (3.3 kΩ / 4.7 kΩ bias, 2.2 MΩ, 4.7 kΩ emitter) with three 1 µF caps, antiparallel diodes across the centre cap, and two legs of 220 kΩ ∥ (4.7 kΩ + 100 kΩ Speed gang) back to the emitter. Intensity (50 kΩ) feeds the lamp driver (100 kΩ collector-base / 47 kΩ base bias, 1 kΩ trimmer + 150 Ω emitter); the 28 V / 40 mA lamp sits between the 21 V reservoir and the driver collector; Cancel shorts the driver base. One lamp lights all four LDRs (light node L1).

sources.title: C. Darabundit, R. Wedelich, P. Bischoff, 'Digital grey box model of the Uni-Vibe effects pedal', DAFx-19: block schematic (Fig. 2), phase-stage analysis with block cap C_DC, measured Table 1 (Cp 15 nF / 220 nF / 470 pF / 4.7 nF; alpha / beta gains; LDR avg / min / max per stage), Speed ≈ 0-7.6 Hz, Cancel cuts lamp power, +21 VDC lamp supply, asymmetric LDR wavetables at 4 Hz

R. G. Keen, 'The Technology of the Univibe' (GeoFex, 1998-2010): preamp, phase stage, final stage, output mixer, LFO / lamp driver and power-supply figures and text (28 V / 40 mA bulb, cold resistance just over 100 Ω, 14-18 VAC secondary, half-wave, 1000 µF / 470 Ω / 100 µF, 20 V LFO-lamp and 16 V audio rails, dual 100K log speed pot, trimmer + 150 Ω lamp emitter, stage DC voltages 4.8 / 3.4 / 11.6 V at 15 V, LFO base 8.6 V)

R. G. Keen, 'UniVibe (model 905, by Unicord, circa 1968)' full schematic, as compiled in 'All Electro-Harmonix Effects' (Experimentalists Anonymous) p. 17: all part values, 2SC828 transistors except the 2SC539 input transistor, CdS 'MXY-7BX4', 470 Ω / 470 Ω and 220 µF / 220 µF / 1000 µF supply filter, 1k lamp trimmer, dual 250K speed pots
2SC828 datasheet summaries (Matsushita/Panasonic): VCEO 25 V, IC 50 mA, hFE 130-520 in Q/R/S grades at 2 mA, fT 220 MHz
Lamp thermal / light law (UNIVIBE_LAMP library model): work/circuit-netlists/wave-c/DEVICES.md §4.2 (Agrawal, tungsten filament model; lamp rerating exponents)

2SC828.note: unverified: no published SPICE card for the Matsushita 2SC828 was found. Generic small-signal values with BF in the datasheet's hFE range (Q 130-260, R 180-360, S 260-520 at 2 mA); the grade fitted to the Uni-Vibe is unknown

UNIVIBE_LAMP_K.note: UNIVIBE_LAMP with Keen's measured cold resistance: 'The cold resistance is just over 100 ohms' for the 28 V / 40 mA bulb, i.e. about 105 Ω / 700 Ω = 0.15 (the library default 1/13.5 = 52 Ω is derived from a 2500 K hot filament). unverified: tau 10 ms (library 20 ms; A) chosen so the lamp's light swings about 250:1 at 4 Hz and full Intensity, which lets the four cells reach DAFx-19's measured min/max with gamma 1.1-1.4; tlambda and thot as the library (A)

2SC539.note: unverified: input transistor type per Keen's schematic ('2SC828 except input transistor' = 2SC539); no SPICE card found, generic values as 2SC828

UV_LDR1.note: unverified fit (D/A): stage 1 (15 nF) cell fitted so that, lit by this netlist's own lamp (UNIVIBE_LAMP_K) at Intensity 1 and Speed 0.9 (LFO 4.0 Hz in ngspice), it spans DAFx-19 Table 1's measured min 12.7 kΩ and max 2.79 MΩ (avg 0.405 MΩ; the fit's geometric mean is close to it). kr 1000 (so n follows a 4 Hz lamp at λ ≈ 1e-4..0.05), rdark 20 MΩ and tau_l 2 s as the library UNIVIBE_LDR. ron is the extrapolated resistance at the lamp's full rated light. Refit if the lamp model changes

controls.label: Speed (foot pedal)
controls.note: Dual 100 kΩ gang in the two LFO legs (220 kΩ ∥ (4.7 kΩ + gang)); 0 = slowest, 1 = fastest. DAFx-19: ≈ 0 to 7.6 Hz over the pedal travel

controls.label: Intensity
controls.note: 50 kΩ Amplitude pot between the LFO output and the lamp driver: sets the lamp's modulation depth, hence the sweep width. Legacy 'Width'

controls.label: Volume
controls.note: 100 kΩ output pot after the Chorus/Vibrato switch. No legacy alias

controls.label: Chorus / Vibrato
controls.note: 0 = Chorus (dry + wet 100 kΩ each), 1 = Vibrato (wet only through 47 kΩ / 220 kΩ). No legacy alias (the legacy 'Mode' 0-4 has no documented mapping)

controls.label: Cancel
controls.note: Heel switch on the foot pedal: shorts the lamp-driver base so the lamp goes dark and the LDRs go to megohms (the 'bypass' of the original; the signal still passes the stages)

controls.label: Lamp bias trim (internal)
controls.note: 1 kΩ trimmer in the lamp-driver emitter (with 150 Ω): sets the idle lamp current, factory-set to a 'medium yellow-orange' glow (Keen). Default 1.0 = trimmer at 0 Ω, i.e. the 150 Ω-only units ('some have only a fixed 150 ohm resistor'): with this lamp model any higher setting leaves the idle lamp near dark (θ < 0.45)

controls.label: Blend
controls.note: No blend control on the Uni-Vibe (the Chorus/Vibrato switch selects fixed mixes); stored only

controls.label: Mode
controls.note: Legacy 0-4 mode selector with no documented mapping onto the Chorus/Vibrato switch; stored only

controls.label: Spread
controls.note: The notch spread is fixed by the 15 nF / 220 nF / 470 pF / 4.7 nF phase caps; stored only

controls.label: Color
controls.note: No color control on the Uni-Vibe; stored only

controls.label: Mix
controls.note: The mix is fixed by the switch (50/50 Chorus, wet-only Vibrato); stored only

controls.label: Stereo
controls.note: Catalogue stereo parameter; mono pedal, stored only

parts.label: Mains transformer secondary (16 Vrms)
parts.note: unverified: Keen measured 14-18 VAC secondaries ('16V a good middle of the road value'); 16 Vrms = 22.6 V peak. The other Keen drawing labels the winding 24 VAC. DAFx-19 reports +21 VDC at the lamp supply, consistent with 16 Vrms half-wave into 1000 µF. The 6.3 V pilot-lamp winding is omitted

parts.label: Secondary winding resistance
parts.note: unverified: transformer secondary winding resistance (not published; a ~10 VA transformer, Keen's estimate). Limits the half-wave charging current

parts.label: Half-wave rectifier
parts.note: Single rectifier diode (Keen: 'half wave rectified'); type not published, silicon 1N4001-class assumed

parts.label: Supply filter cap 1
parts.note: unverified: 220 µF in the Keen full schematic (EA compilation); Keen's GeoFex supply figure shows 100 µF

parts.label: Supply filter resistor 2
parts.note: Keen's GeoFex article text says 100 Ω RC sections; both Keen drawings show 470 Ω

parts.label: Audio rail cap (≈ 16-17 V)
parts.note: unverified: 220 µF (EA compilation) vs 100 µF (GeoFex figure)

parts.label: Input 2 mixing resistor (jack unplugged)
parts.note: unverified: input 2's shorting jack grounds its 22 kΩ when nothing is plugged in (switch contact drawn to ground in both Keen drawings), so input 1 sees 22k into 22k ∥ 47k (−7.8 dB). Keen's article counts only the 22k + 47k (69 kΩ) load

parts.label: Compensation cap (Keen: C4, Q2 collector to ground)
Q3 split emitter (feedback)
parts.note: 3.3k per both Keen drawings (his article text says 3.9k). Closed-loop gain ≈ 1 + 3.3k/1.2k = 3.75

parts.label: Volume
parts.note: unverified taper: 100 kΩ per Keen; audio taper assumed

parts.label: LFO amplitude limiter
parts.note: unverified type: two antiparallel diodes across the centre cap (Keen); silicon small-signal assumed

parts.label: Speed (foot pedal), gang A
parts.note: unverified value: Keen's article: 'dual 100K log taper pot in the footpedal ... mechanically turned the correct direction'; his full schematic and its caption say dual 250K. Rheostat with R = 100k·(1 − t(x)) on the C taper, i.e. the log pot turned so that speed rises with x

parts.label: Speed (foot pedal), gang B
parts.note: unverified value: Keen's article: 'dual 100K log taper pot in the footpedal ... mechanically turned the correct direction'; his full schematic and its caption say dual 250K. Rheostat with R = 100k·(1 − t(x)) on the C taper, i.e. the log pot turned so that speed rises with x

parts.label: LFO start kick
parts.note: Simulation aid, not in the unit: 1 mV at 4 Hz through 10 MΩ into the LFO network node n1, as power-up transients start the real oscillator. Its DC value sits at n1's nominal bias (≈ the Darlington emitter, 10.5 V) so the 10 MΩ draws almost no DC (a 1 V mismatch shifts n1 by ≤ 10 mV through the ≤ 105 kΩ leg). Feeding the kick into the 2.2 MΩ-biased base instead would pull the LFO bias by volts

parts.label: Intensity (Amplitude)
parts.note: unverified taper: 50 kΩ per Keen; linear assumed

parts.label: Lamp-driver base resistor
parts.note: 47k on both drawings: Keen's full schematic (All Electro-Harmonix Effects.pdf p.17 @200 dpi, crop (100,1260)-(1400,1500): '10u - 47k' into the lamp driver) and the Univox 915 factory drawing (univibe_915.pdf p.1 @400 dpi, crop (150,700)-(750,1500) rotated: '47K'). Was 4.7k (2026-11-12 fix): that over-drove the lamp, so Intensity saturated at half travel

parts.label: Cancel (heel switch: shorts the lamp-driver base)
Lamp bias trimmer
parts.note: unverified: Keen: 500 Ω-1 kΩ trimmer plus 150 Ω ('some original models have only the trimpot, some have only a fixed 150 ohm'); his full schematic shows 1k
